title: WOS Evolution Spec — §4 Load-Bearing Abstractions
subtitle: Force-directed vocabulary graph of the 12 locked abstractions

sections.label: §4
sections.title: Load-Bearing Abstractions
sections.content:
The 12 terms below are **status: LOCKED** in the WOS Evolution Spec §4. Each node in the graph represents one abstraction. Hover or click a node to see its definition. Use the filter buttons to narrow to register-tier concepts only or include parameter nodes.

**Node tiers:**

- **Concepts** (large circles) — top-level architectural abstractions
- **Parameters** (medium circles) — components that parametrize a concept
- **Cross-register** (dashed circles) — failure modes or cross-cutting concerns

**Edge types:**

- Solid lines — pipeline flow (hub)
- Light solid — parameter relationship
- Dashed — cross-register dependency

nodes.def: Typed PrescriptionObject output by Prescriber (not prose string). The structured signal that drives executor behavior.

examples.text: Prescriber emits a typed object with register targets and hypothesis type — not a freeform instruction string.

nodes.def: Scored outcome for a specific hypothesis after a UoW closes. The fundamental unit of feedback in the learning loop.

examples.text: After a UoW completes, the steward scores the hypothesis: success, failure, or partial.

nodes.def: Persistent store mapping (register, hypothesis) → (n_successes, n_failures, n_partial). The memory substrate for learning.

examples.text: Each hypothesis type accumulates verdict history across all UoWs in that register.

nodes.def: Component that reads the Verdict Accumulator and biases Prescriber toward high-accuracy hypothesis types.

examples.text: If 'decompose' hypotheses score 80% success in the code register, Selector upweights that type.

nodes.def: Governor output: workstream emphasis weights + register targets. Portfolio-level, not UoW-level.

examples.text: Governor sets 60% capacity toward infra register, 40% toward product — Prescriber reads this when selecting next UoW.

nodes.def: Category of improvement action. Two kinds: scaffold lever (IFTTT/config) and learning lever (selector biasing).

examples.text: A scaffold lever adds an IFTTT rule. A learning lever reweights Selector output for a register.

nodes.def: Multi-tier execution population: Tier 1 (ephemeral), Tier 2 (persistent domain), Tier 3 (external).

examples.text: A Tier 2 executor holds domain context across sessions; a Tier 1 executor is spun up and torn down per UoW.

nodes.def: Per-workstream multiplier on issue promotion speed, derived from Portfolio Prescription.

examples.text: A workstream with high Portfolio emphasis gets a larger Germination Bias, surfacing its issues faster.

nodes.def: Class A = auto-apply within bounded scope. Class B = requires Dan's explicit approval before applying.

examples.text: Adding an IFTTT rule for a known pattern is Class A. Changing the Prescriber weighting schema is Class B.

nodes.def: Typed interface for executor capability matching and UoW claiming. Governs how UoWs are assigned to executors.

examples.text: An executor declares its capability set; the Claim Protocol matches UoW requirements against declared capabilities.

nodes.def: wos_capacity_available inbox message fired when an executor slot frees. Triggers next UoW dispatch.

examples.text: When a Tier 1 executor closes, it fires Capacity Event; the dispatcher polls for pending UoWs to fill the slot.

nodes.def: Failure mode: Prescriber and Executor optimize against the same verdict context, reaching a Nash equilibrium rather than true improvement.

examples.text: Prescriber biases toward fast-completing UoWs because Executor scores them highest — metric gaming, not real progress.
